title: Diagonal counit identity for a flat proper morphism
statement: Let S and X be Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], let f:X\to S be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let \Delta:X\to X\times_S X be the diagonal [def-pc-base-change], and suppose a is a right adjoint to Rf_* and c is a right adjoint to R\Delta_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism \mathcal O_X\cong c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*a(\mathcal O_S)) in the derived category of quasi-coherent complexes on X.

source.place: Tag 0E2Q (diagonal counit identity, under flat proper hypotheses)

proof.text: Form the cartesian square P=X\times_S X with the projection pr_2:P\to X chosen as the base change of f and pr_1:P\to X the other projection, so pr_2\circ\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X. Since f is proper, pr_2 is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence of finite type; since X is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] shows that P is Noetherian. The right-adjoint existence statement for Noetherian schemes [lem-pc-noetherian-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint] therefore supplies a right adjoint b to R(pr_2)_*. Since f is proper it is separated, so \Delta is a closed immersion and hence proper (Stacks Tags 01KH, 01W6), and pr_2 is proper; as pr_2\circ\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X, the composition isomorphism for derived direct images of proper morphisms of Noetherian schemes [lem-pc-proper-derived-direct-image-composition] gives R(pr_2)_*\circ R\Delta_*\cong R(\operatorname{id}_X)_*=\operatorname{id}. Hence the pasted adjunction and uniqueness of right adjoints [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] give a canonical isomorphism c\circ b\cong\operatorname{id} on the quasi-coherent derived category. Evaluating at \mathcal O_X gives \mathcal O_X\cong c(b(\mathcal O_X)).

source.place: Tag 0E2P, proof of Lemma 48.12.8, first equality and the cartesian square

proof.text: Since f is proper it is of finite type, and a morphism of finite type to the Noetherian scheme S is of finite presentation (Stacks Tag 01TX); so f is flat, proper and of finite presentation, as the following statement requires. The base-change formula for the right adjoint in this cartesian square [lem-sc-smooth-proper-diagonal-basechange-upper-shriek] identifies b(\mathcal O_X) canonically with L\operatorname{pr}_1^*a(\mathcal O_S). Applying c to that isomorphism and composing with Step 1 yields the required canonical isomorphism \mathcal O_X\cong c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*a(\mathcal O_S)).
